summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for evaluation of persistent chest pressure and shortness of breath, initially noted after his primary care physician identified ST elevations on a prior EKG. He underwent cardiac catheterization, which revealed in-stent restenosis of the OM1 artery, successfully treated with a drug-eluting stent. His symptoms resolved post-procedure. During admission, he was also diagnosed with an infected tooth (#21), for which he was started on antibiotics, pain medication, and a chlorhexidine mouth rinse, with plans for outpatient extraction. He remained on anticoagulation for prior pulmonary embolism, bridged with Lovenox post-procedure. His diabetes, hypertension, and heart failure were managed throughout. He was discharged home with a walker, new medications including Plavix, and close follow-up instructions.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Acute apical periodontitis of pulpal origin
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
